scored_papers.title: Planckian bounds on thermalization times of strongly coupled open quantum systems
scored_papers.abstract: We consider whether the thermalization of strongly coupled open quantum systems, whose equilibrium state is the mean-force Gibbs (MFG) state, is constrained by a fundamental Planckian time scale, $\hbar/k_B T$. By requiring that the same process thermalizes a family of nearby system Hamiltonians, we obtain a lower bound on the thermalization time, irrespective of the specific system-bath dynamics. The bound depends only on the distinguishability of the corresponding MFG states, and can therefore be computed from equilibrium properties alone. In its simplest form, it requires only a static susceptibility and an equilibrium variance of a system observable. We characterize this bound from weak to strong coupling in exactly solvable fermionic models, in the spin-boson model, and in a spin coupled to a two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet. These models show that strong coupling can lift the Planckian constraint when the MFG state retains little information about the system Hamiltonian, while preserving it when that information is carried by system observables with substantial equilibrium fluctuations at frequencies below $k_B T/\hbar$. The bound is complementary to open-system speed limits, since it constrains the acquisition of information rather than the preparation of the target, and can remain informative at strong coupling even when the latter become trivial.

scored_papers.title: Rugosity as a measurement-induced relative entropy
scored_papers.abstract: Quantum-state rugosity quantifies the departure of a quantum state from the flat superposition associated with a prescribed basis. We show that rugosity equals the classical relative entropy generated by the binary flat-state measurement. This identity gives two hypothesis-testing interpretations. Rugosity is the asymptotic discrimination exponent under repeated flat-state measurements and the exact finite-copy exponent under unrestricted quantum testing with zero type-I error. For smoothly parametrized states, we relate its local variation to the Fisher information accessible through the prescribed measurement. Using the local expansion of quantum relative entropy, we derive a bound on rugosity sensitivity in terms of the entropy-production susceptibility of a subsequent thermal reset. This susceptibility is given by the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori Fisher information. Finally, we formulate a measurement-dependent quantum speed limit whose endpoint distinguishability is determined by rugosity. These results connect quantum-state rugosity with statistical discrimination, thermal reset, and the geometry of experimentally accessible probability distributions.

scored_papers.summary: 🧮 rugosity が二値の平坦状態測定の古典相対エントロピーに等しいことを示し、仮説検定の指数として解釈。局所変化を Fisher 情報と結び、終点の識別可能性を rugosity で決める速度限界を定式化。
